openIssues.title: Before v1: revoke the agent's unattended gh pr merge permission
openIssues.body:
`.claude/settings.local.json` grants `Bash(gh pr merge:*)` so the agent can merge without a prompt per PR. That was added deliberately on 2026-08-18 to unblock a long autonomous backlog run, and it is appropriate for a solo-maintainer tool in early development. It is not appropriate once this has users.

Before tagging v1.0.0, remove the rule:

```json
"allow": [
  "Bash(gh pr merge --admin *)",
  "Bash(gh pr merge:*)"     <-- delete this line
]
```

The narrower `Bash(gh pr merge --admin *)` entry predates this and is a separate decision; it exists because release PRs cannot pass their required check (see #366) and so can only be merged with `--admin`. Fixing #366 removes the reason for that one too, at which point both can go and every merge returns to being an explicit human action.

Worth doing at the same time: re-read `CLAUDE.md`'s standing rule that a passing pipeline is not permission to merge. This grant is a deliberate, scoped exception to it, and v1 is the right moment for the exception to lapse.

I think that the dbus error may be related.  This seems to have been happening for maybe around a week for me.

Using Plasma 6.3 on Debian trixie now and in this log, had tried it on an Ubuntu machine too (Plasma 6.6) with same behaviour.

openIssues.body:
### Can you reproduce this bug on the Microsoft Teams web app (https://teams.microsoft.com)?

Not applicable

### Describe the bug

With notificationMethod 'electron', clicking a notification while its banner is on screen opens Teams, but clicking the same notification later from the GNOME notification list (top panel) does nothing.

### What package are you using?

deb

### Version

2.24.0

### Reproduction steps

1. Set `"notificationMethod": "electron"` (also tested with `"notifications": { "timeoutType": "never", "electron": { "clickAction": "restore" } }`)
2. Receive a chat message while Teams is in the background; let the banner go away without clicking it
3. Wait a little, then open the GNOME notification list from the top panel and click the Teams for Linux notification
4. Nothing happens: the window is not shown/raised and the chat is not opened

### Expected Behavior

1. Clicking the notification from the notification list behaves the same as clicking the banner: the window is shown/restored and Teams opens the sending conversation

### Debug

No relevant log output: when it fails, the click handler never runs, so `[NOTIFICATIONS] Notification clicked` is never logged.

Likely cause (from reading `app/notifications/service.js` on `main`): in `#showNotification` the `Notification` instance (`const notification = new Notification(notificationConfig)`, ~line 89) is only held by a local variable. Once the function returns nothing references it, so it can be garbage-collected together with its `click`/`close` listeners. The native notification stays in the GNOME list, but its click no longer reaches any JS handler. Clicking the banner works because it happens before GC runs. This is the usual Electron advice to keep a reference to notifications you want to receive events from.

### Additional context

Possible fix: keep live notifications in a module/instance-level `Set` (or `Map` keyed by `notificationId`), add on `show()`, and remove on `close` (and maybe after `click`), with a size cap like `MAX_TRACKED_NOTIFICATIONS` in `notificationBridge.js` since Electron does not always emit `close`. The renderer-side `NotificationBridge` already keeps its entries after close for exactly this case, so only the main-process side drops the reference.

Environment: Ubuntu, GNOME on X11 (`--ozone-platform=x11`), deb package 2.24.0. The relevant code is unchanged on `main` / 2.26.0.

openIssues.title: Move the presence overlay option to `tray.showStatus` once `tray` is no longer a rename target (gate A, #2842)

labels.name: awaiting user feedback
labels.description: Waiting for user to confirm they still need this feature

openIssues.body:
Follow-up from #3102, as requested by @IsmaelMartinez there.

## What

#3102 overlays the Teams presence status on the **tray icon** on the platforms that have no Dock (macOS keeps it on the Dock), and reuses the existing `media.showStatusOnDockIcon` as the switch instead of adding the option where ADR-025 puts it, `tray.showStatus`.

The reused name has outgrown what it says: the setting now means "overlay the presence status on the app icon — the Dock on macOS, the tray icon elsewhere".

## Why not now

`tray` is still a rename-target namespace (`tray.enabled`, `tray.icon`, `tray.iconType`, `tray.useMutationTitleLogic` are live entries until 2.30.0), so a new leaf there trips the gate A boundary suite in `tests/unit/configRenames.test.js`:

> `tray.showStatus is not a rename target, so tray is no longer safe`

A config file that sets one leaf of such a namespace also replaces the object wholesale and drops the declared defaults of its siblings (see the #2842 write-up in that file).

## When the window closes

1. Declare `tray.showStatus` in `app/config/options.js` and move the description out of `media`.
2. Keep `media.showStatusOnDockIcon` working as a legacy alias. Worth noting for whoever picks this up: the alias is **nested → nested** (`media.showStatusOnDockIcon` → `tray.showStatus`), while `RENAMES` in `app/config/renames.js` is flat → nested only, so this needs either a small extension of the table or a dedicated legacy lookup.
3. The read site is a single helper — `wantsPresenceStatus()` in `app/browser/tools/presenceColors.js`, also used through `wantsPresenceOverlay` by the multi-account aggregator in `app/index.js` — so the code change is that one helper plus the alias.
4. `npm run generate-config-docs` for `docs-site/docs/configuration-generated.md` and `docs-site/static/config-schema.json`.

No new config surface: it renames an existing option, so configs that set it today keep working through the alias.

openIssues.title: microphoneControlState never leaves "unmuted": track.enabled is not flipped by current Teams on mute

labels.name: release ready
labels.description: Fix merged to main, included in the next release

openIssues.body:
### Can you reproduce this bug on the Microsoft Teams web app?

Not applicable — this is about the wrapper's own state detection (`speakingIndicator.js` → `microphone-state-changed` → MQTT / D-Bus `microphoneControlState`), which the web app does not have.

### Describe the bug

With the new D-Bus control service enabled (#0b63f8d), `microphoneControlState` stays `"unmuted"` (and `microphoneState` `"silent"`) for the whole call, no matter how many times the mic is muted and unmuted from the Teams toolbar. No `MicrophoneChanged` / `MicrophoneControlChanged` / `StateChanged` signal is emitted on a toggle. Teams' own button correctly shows *Unmute* (i.e. muted) while the service reports unmuted.

Call state, camera state and the actions themselves (`ToggleMute`, `ToggleVideo`, `LeaveCall`, …) all work; it is only the mute **observation** that is stuck.

Cause, as far as I can tell: `speakingIndicator.js` (`#micStateFor`) decides "muted" from `RTCRtpSender.track.enabled === false` on the outgoing audio sender, documented in the file header as "authoritative and unambiguous". On the current Teams web client that flag no longer flips when the user mutes — the track stays `enabled === true` — so the detector only ever reaches the `silent`/`speaking` branches. (The camera check uses the same test and does work, since Teams still disables the video track on camera-off.)

Worth noting: #2465 records that `track.enabled` polling for the mic had already been tried in March and "did not reliably reflect Teams' mute state", and was dropped in favour of the `media-source.audioLevel` path. The `track.enabled` check seems to have come back later as the primary mute signal, and it does not hold on today's Teams.

Since the maintainers' earlier audioLevel traces in #2465 did show `silent → muted` transitions, this may depend on the Teams build / rollout ring. Here it is 100% reproducible across calls and restarts.

### What package are you using?

RPM (`teams-for-linux-2.25.0-1.x86_64`), Fedora 44 Workstation, COSMIC desktop (Wayland, app running with `--ozone-platform=x11`).

### Version

2.25.0

### Reproduction steps

1. `config.json`: `{ "dbusControl": { "enabled": true } }`, restart the app.
2. Join any meeting; confirm `inCall` is true:
   ```
   busctl --user call com.github.IsmaelMartinez.teams_for_linux \
     /com/github/IsmaelMartinez/teams_for_linux \
     com.github.IsmaelMartinez.teams_for_linux.Control GetState
   ```
3. In another terminal, watch the service's signals:
   ```
   busctl --user monitor --match "type='signal',interface='com.github.IsmaelMartinez.teams_for_linux.Control'"
   ```
4. Mute and unmute the microphone from the Teams toolbar several times.
5. Call `GetState` again.

### Expected Behavior

`microphoneControlState` flips between `"muted"` and `"unmuted"` on each toggle, with a `MicrophoneControlChanged` signal each time, matching the state Teams' own mic button shows.

### Debug

30-second trace with a filtered monitor, muting/unmuting throughout (nothing was emitted; before and after are identical):

```
# 2026-10-13T09:06:22-07:00 GetState before:
s "{"presenceStatus":"busy","presenceStatusCode":2,"inCall":true,"incomingCall":false,"incomingCallCaller":null,"cameraEnabled":false,"microphoneState":"silent","microphoneControlState":"unmuted","screenSharing":false,"meetingStarted":false}"
# monitor 30s (toggle mic in Teams several times):
<no signals>
# 2026-10-13T09:06:52-07:00 GetState after:
s "{"presenceStatus":"busy","presenceStatusCode":2,"inCall":true,"incomingCall":false,"incomingCallCaller":null,"cameraEnabled":false,"microphoneState":"silent","microphoneControlState":"unmuted","screenSharing":false,"meetingStarted":false}"
```

An unfiltered `busctl --user monitor com.github.IsmaelMartinez.teams_for_linux` over the same window showed only systemd cgroup traffic from the process — no `Control` interface signals at all.

### Additional context

Possible signals to try in `#micStateFor`, in case any of them does still move on current Teams: `track.muted === true`, `track.readyState === 'ended'`, the audio sender having its track replaced/`null`ed (`sender.track == null`), or the `RTCOutboundRtpStreamStats`/`media-source` stat disappearing. Happy to run a patched build against this setup and report back what the DOM/WebRTC actually does on mute here — the `[SPEAKING_INDICATOR] State:` log lines are easy to collect.

openIssues.title: 2.22.0: does not exit on SIGTERM under Flatpak (45s shutdown delay)

labels.name: blocked
labels.description: This issue depends on external projects

openIssues.body:
## Summary

Since 2.22.0 the app does not exit on SIGTERM, which delays system shutdown by 45s, and its CPU use grows with session length rather than staying flat.

Both appeared on the same update. The previous build does neither on the same machine.

## Environment

- teams-for-linux 2.22.0, Flatpak from Flathub (commit `a7c3e840`, later rebuild `b63da975`)
- Fedora 44, KDE Plasma 6.7.5, Wayland
- Kernel 7.2.7
- systemd user manager, `DefaultTimeoutStopUSec=45s`

## 1. No exit on SIGTERM

On every shutdown, one Teams scope exits immediately and the other has to be killed after the timeout:

```
13:25:13.484  Stopping app-flatpak-...teams_for_linux-3589722297.scope...
13:25:13.650  Stopped  app-flatpak-...teams_for_linux-3021391478.scope      (170ms)
13:25:58.710  app-flatpak-...teams_for_linux-3589722297.scope: Stopping timed out. Killing.
13:25:58.711  Killing process 5907 (bwrap) with signal SIGKILL
13:25:58.711  Killing process 5908 (teams-for-linux) with signal SIGKILL
13:25:58.760  Failed with result 'timeout'
```

It is the only stop-job timeout in the boot. Everything after it completes in 2s.

Reproduced on two consecutive shutdowns. A third session, still running the pre-2.22.0 build in memory, exited cleanly.

Possibly related to #2743, which replaced the hard exit on SIGTERM with a queued graceful quit.

## 2. CPU grows with session length

Figures are systemd cgroup accounting for the Teams scope, taken from the shutdown log of each session:

| build | session length | Teams CPU | share of one core | shutdown |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pre-2.22.0 | 2h 44m | 9m 46s | 6.0% | clean |
| 2.22.0 | 5h 45m | 1h 3m | 18.4% | timeout |
| 2.22.0 | 8h 30m | 4h 46m | 56.1% | timeout |

Constant overhead would hold the percentage roughly flat. It rises with uptime, which suggests something accumulating rather than a fixed cost.

The middle row is the control: Flathub deployed 2.22.0 mid-session at 05:17, but a deploy does not replace a running instance, so that session kept executing the older build until it exited.

## Note

The app was otherwise idle in all three sessions (no calls, no screen sharing). Teams accounted for over half of all user-session CPU in the 8.5h case.

Happy to supply full journal extracts, run with debug logging, or test a patch.

openIssues.title: [Feat]: Upgrade to Electron 44 and drop the armv7l packages

labels.name: release ready
labels.description: Fix merged to main, included in the next release

labels.name: dependencies
labels.description: Pull requests that update a dependency file

openIssues.body:
Electron 43 is EOL on 2027-01-05. 44 has been stable since 2026-08-25 (44.4.3 now, EOL 2027-03-02) and ships no 32-bit builds, so the bump means dropping armv7l; #2927 parked that decision here. Dependabot is ignoring 44 since #2962, so this is a manual PR or a reopen of that one.

## Changes

- Drop armv7l: the `--armv7l` flags and the two armv7l scripts in `package.json`; the `linux_arm` job in build.yml; `snap-armv7l` in snap.yml and `snap-candidate-armv7l` in snap-release.yml (both, they are parallel copies); the two blocks in comment-artifacts.yml; the `armhf` entries in `scripts/patchSnapDesktopLauncher.js`; the ADR 011 table row.
- `joinMeeting()` (`app/menus/index.js:643`) uses `clipboard.readText()` synchronously; 44 makes it a Promise, so await it.
- 44 lifts the libunity gate on `setBadgeCount` / `setProgressBar`. `launcherEntryEmitter.js` exists to bypass that gate, so badge and progress may now emit twice. Measure with `dbus-monitor` on GNOME, then retire or gate the emitter.
- Release notes: a `!` commit cuts 3.0.0, a plain bump hides the platform drop. Decide.
- Everything else in the 44 breaking-change list greps clean.

## What we lose

armv7l is 2 to 2.5% of Linux downloads per stable release (123 of 4832 on v2.20.1). Those users stay on the last 43 build; armv7l AppImage installs will only ever see "Failed to check for updates", so any notice has to ship on 43 before the bump. macOS 12 is dropped too.

## What we gain

Tray icons on desktops that address StatusNotifierItem by unique D-Bus name, badge and progress without libunity, Chromium 152. Target a matured 44.x as with the last two bumps.

openIssues.title: [Feat]: Opt-in secondary window for the same account (chat while in a call)
openIssues.body:
### Describe the feature

Opt-in "New window" action that opens a second lightweight Teams window on the same account/session, so a call can stay on one monitor while chatting in another. Like a second browser tab, without moving the running call.

### Motivation

During a meeting with screen sharing, the shared content fills the main window and there is no way to follow or answer chats from other people without hiding the call. The Windows client solves this natively (pop-out windows); on Linux the wrapper has a single window.

Both earlier requests were closed as not planned, but the blockers cited do not apply to this proposal:

- #2499 (separate call window): the call lives in the renderer (WebRTC tracks, signalling, UI) and cannot be moved to another `BrowserWindow` without tearing it down. Agreed, this proposal does not move the call. The call stays in the main window; the secondary window is an independent Teams instance for chat.
- #1984 (multiple windows for one account): the concern was that Microsoft's web app would not allow multiple instances of the same account, plus the risk of Microsoft changing behaviour again. I re-tested this today and the web app does allow it (see Additional context).

Since teams-for-linux wraps exactly this web app, a second `BrowserWindow` sharing the session partition should behave like that second tab.

Proposed scope, deliberately minimal:

- **Opt-in** via config (e.g. `secondaryWindow.enabled`, default `false`), so nobody's setup changes unless they ask for it.
- A menu entry / configurable shortcut ("New window") that opens a `BrowserWindow` on the **same session partition** as the active profile, loading the Teams URL.
- The secondary window runs a **lightweight preload**: none of the singleton browser tools (title observer / tray & badge counter, notification handling, MQTT status, idle, etc.). Those stay owned by the main window, so there are no duplicated badges or toasts.
- Closing the secondary window just closes it: it never minimises to tray, never quits the app, and its bounds are not persisted.
- Graceful degradation: if Microsoft ever re-introduces a single-instance lock, the secondary window simply shows whatever the web app shows (as a browser tab would). No wrapper logic depends on the lock being absent.

Out of scope on purpose: pop-out of the running call, pop-out chats attached to the main renderer, multi-window state sync.

If the maintainers are open to this scope, I am happy to implement it and submit a PR with tests and docs. I would rather agree on the approach here first than send an unrequested PR for a feature that was closed twice.

### Alternatives

- **QuickChat** (the workaround shipped for #1984): covers "send a quick message during a call", but it only reaches contacts with prior message history (Graph API limitation noted in #1984) and does not show an ongoing conversation. A secondary window covers reading and following conversations, channels, and anything else the web app offers, with zero API surface of our own.
- **Using the browser / PWA alongside the wrapper**: works today, but means running Teams twice with two different notification and badge sources, and defeats the point of having a dedicated client.
- **Waiting for Microsoft to add pop-out to the web app**: possible, but there is no sign of it, and the proposal is designed so that it does not conflict with it if it ever arrives (opt-in, no dependency on internal web app behaviour).

### Additional context

Evidence that the web app allows concurrent instances of the same account (tested 2026-09-10):

Environment: Ubuntu 24.04, GNOME 46 (Xorg), Google Chrome, `teams.cloud.microsoft`, work account (M365). teams-for-linux 2.20.0 (snap).

1. Started a meeting alone ("Meet now") in a regular browser tab.
2. With the call in progress, opened the same account in (a) the installed Teams PWA and (b) a second regular tab.
3. Result in both cases: the second instance loads normally, chats can be opened, messages sent and received, **while the call keeps running in the first instance**. No "Teams is open in another window" lock, no forced hand-over.

So the "one active instance" restriction reported in #1984 is not in effect (anymore, or at least not for this tenant/account type).

Related: #1984, #2499, #2938 (PiP controls during calls, a different surface for a similar need).

openIssues.title: [Feat]: Enable auth.webauthn.enabled by default on Linux

labels.name: blocked
labels.description: This issue depends on external projects

openIssues.body:
### What

Flip `auth.webauthn.enabled` from `false` to `true` so the WebAuthn interception runs by default on Linux. The flag stays, so anyone can opt back out.

### Why

Electron ships no WebAuthn backend on Linux ([electron/electron#24573](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/24573)). With the flag off, a `publicKey` request from Microsoft's login page goes to Chromium's stock path, nothing ever opens, and the sign-in screen sits spinning until the request times out. There is no escape link on that screen.

With the flag on and a security key present, `resolveDevice` in `app/webauthn/fido2Backend.js` throws `NotAllowedError` as soon as device discovery comes back empty, and Microsoft renders its "We couldn't sign you in" screen, which carries a working "Sign in another way" link.

That is no longer the whole story on `main`. #2917 added `discoverableGet` to the PIN pre-collect condition in `app/webauthn/index.js`, and Microsoft's "security key" route sends no `allowCredentials`, so a user with no key now meets a PIN dialog before `resolveDevice` ever runs. Slothinger's screenshot in #2912 was taken on 2.18.1, where the pre-collect fired only when `userVerification` was required.

#2912 has this from both sides. Slothinger was stuck on the spinning screen with the flag off, and got through in seconds once it was on, despite having no security key at all and signing in with a password plus a phone call.

### What changes, by user

- Has a USB security key and `fido2-tools`: working sign-in instead of a hang.
- No security key: an instant error screen with the escape link, instead of a long spin. See the caveat above, this no longer holds unchanged on `main`.
- No `fido2-tools` installed, which includes Flatpak since the manifest does not ship it: `initialize()` returns before registering the IPC handlers, so the call fails in about a millisecond with "No handler registered", surfaced as `NotAllowedError`.
- Corporate SSO origins outside `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (#2931): only subframes fall through. `injectIntoFrame` returns early on a disallowed origin, but the main-frame preload has no origin check, so a top-level federated IdP is intercepted, rejected in the main process, and surfaces to the page as a `SecurityError`. #2931's own log line shows exactly this. Now fixed in #2945, which is why this should land first.
- macOS and Windows: unchanged, the override is Linux only.

### Risks

Promoting a beta to the default path means a bug in our fido2 code reaches everyone rather than volunteers. The behaviour it replaces is a hang with nothing to click, so the floor is low, but it is a real change in blast radius.

It also spawns `fido2-tools` per ceremony and shows the touch prompt window added in 2.18.0 to people who were not expecting it.

Worth deciding alongside #2931, since the origin allowlist governs who the interception reaches at all.

### Alternative considered

Keeping the default off and adding a fail-fast path for the disabled case. This is strictly more work for a worse outcome. The interception is two layers, the preload for the main frame and `webFrameMain` injection for subframes (`app/webauthn/index.js`), both gated on the same flag, so it would mean rebuilding both purely to return an error, with no security key support to show for it.

There is now a smaller option than either. Running `resolveDevice` before `collectPin` restores the immediate failure for a machine with no key, since collecting a PIN for a device nobody has discovered is backwards. That recovers the behaviour this issue was written to generalise, without changing any default.

Refs #2912, #2714

openIssues.title: [Feat]: Passkey bridging to work around missing Passkey support

labels.name: awaiting user feedback
labels.description: Waiting for user to confirm they still need this feature

openIssues.body:
### Describe the feature

As discussed in #2714, there should be a way to configure a custom plugin / wrapper script / etc. for Passkey handling.

### Motivation

Right now, there is no unified Passkey solution on Linux like there is on Windows with Windows Hello and on MacOS with iCloud Keychain. 

Teams-for-Linux supports physical FIDO2 keys through the fido2-tools application, but it does not support Passkeys stored in 3rd-party password managers like KeepassXC, Bitwarden or 1Password. 

The fido2-tools only require the client data hash, but most other systems / password managers require the full client data JSON which is currently not provided by Teams-for-Linux. 

I would like to have a feature in Teams-for-Linux that'd allow people to write their own wrapper scripts to make Teams-for-Linux interface with their particular password manager for Passkey support, until [Passkey support on Linux](https://github.com/linux-credentials) has matured enough to be natively integrated.

That would mean that the path to the binary / binaries should be configurable in the config file instead of hardcoded to the fido2-tools, and there should be a way for Teams-for-Linux to pass the entire clientDataJSON to this application, not just the clientDataHash.

### Alternatives

- Using a physical passkey, but then I'd have to have a separate key just for Teams ...
- Waiting for https://github.com/linux-credentials, but I assume it'll still take quite a long time for this solution to be integrated into Linux distributions, and with Microsoft starting to push Passkeys more and more, I'd like to have a faster solution.

### Additional context

See previous conversation at #2714.

The design is settled in ADR-020, this issue only tracks delivery.

## Status

Per-profile `WebContentsView`s, top-right switcher overlay, `Profiles` menu with Add / Switch / Manage flows, `Ctrl+Alt+1…5` shortcuts, first-run Profile 0 migration, the six Phase 1 `profile-*` IPC channels, plus the audit-table shared-state migrations.

openIssues.title: Governance: SHA-pinned actions and least-privilege workflow permissions standard
openIssues.body:
Add a portfolio standard for SHA-pinned GitHub Actions and least-privilege workflow `permissions:`. A survey on 2026-09-26 found 13 of 14 repos with `uses:` refs not pinned to a 40-hex SHA, and 21 workflows across 11 repos without a top-level `permissions:`.

- The worst cases are bonnie-wee-plot (22/25 unpinned), skill-sources (15/17), sound3fy (14/16), generator-atlassian-compass-event-catalog (13/15, including a mutable `changesets/action@master` in its release workflow) and ai-model-advisor (13/16). Only repo-butler and ismaelmartinez.me.uk are fully pinned.
- Proposed shape: a detector counting unpinned refs and missing `permissions:` per repo, plus a workflow lint (zizmor or actionlint, present on 0/14) to keep them fixed. Dependabot's `github-actions` ecosystem already bumps pinned SHAs with the version comment, so pinning costs no upkeep.
- Pinning rewrites files the butler did not author, which is an ADR-013 content transformation. Decide whether this is a templated apply or per-repo PRs before building, and sequence it after #429.

openIssues.body:
### ▶ Resume here ("continue with what we were doing")
Last updated 2026-10-07. Waves 1 and 2 are merged; wave 3 code items are done (#420, #421, #422). Owner decisions #423, #427, #428 and the #452 tier rule are settled, and #452's presentation follow-up #477 is done (#482, #484, #485, #486, #493). Follow-ups #440 and #481 shipped (#489, #488). `CLAUDE.md` is now `AGENTS.md` (#492), and onboarding writes to `AGENTS.md` (#491). #424–#426 are on hold, and the AGENTS.md restructure waits only on those three.
1. If a `repo-butler/roadmap-update-*` PR is open, review its diff (every cited PR must exist and be merged) and merge it first.
2. Next item: the **AGENTS.md restructure** (formerly CLAUDE.md), once the owner decisions in step 4 are answered (it documents their outcome). It collects the `CLAUDE.md delta:` lines from the bodies of PRs #430–#437, #443–#451, #453, #456 and #458, with an invariant checklist before and after. Review follow-ups from #456/#458, filed 2026-09-30 and not part of this pass: #459 (template-hash list copied three times), #460 (`observe()` positional `Promise.all`), #461 (campaign parity test does not call `computeCampaigns`), #462 (codeowners owner not validated), #463 (workflow filenames duplicated between detection and templates), #464 (npm runner flags untested).
3. Per item: a worktree off `origin/main`, tests first with a mutation check, then the full `npm test`, a PR with `Refs:`, and `/address-pr-comments`. The owner merges. Tick the item below after it merges. The CI floors are `MIN_TESTS: 1700` and `MIN_TEST_FILES: 44` (45 files exist after #456); lower them only on purpose.
4. Owner decisions on hold: #424 (reusable Action vs own-portfolio tool), and #425/#426, which the owner links to #424 (monitor watches only this repo because `monitor.js` reads `context.repo`; the PROPOSE soak's 0 cross-repo routes come from IDEATE targeting repo-butler itself and the one-repo `propose-targets` allow-list, not from App installation — the App is installed on all 27 public repos).

Plan of record for the 2026-09-26 simplification pass. Five parallel read-only audits (pipeline core; governance/apply; reporting/MCP/infra; docs/usability; tests/CI/dead code) were followed by three adversarial reviews (safety, executability, value) that corrected two diagnoses and reshaped the waves. Base `origin/main` @ `8b9065f0`; CI baseline 1716 tests.

The code is mostly well factored — providers, prompt wrapping, the MCP tool table and the test seams are fine. The real problems are defects hiding behind duplication (one copy hardened, the others not), safety nets that look active but are inert, and sprawl in two large files, a 50 KB CLAUDE.md and drifted docs.

### Wave 1 — defects and inert nets (parallel, disjoint files)
Status 2026-09-27: all eight MERGED after independent review (roadmap PR #439 merged before #433); main CI 1815 tests, 0 fail. Superseded note: A trial merge of all eight onto `8b9065f0` is conflict-free and runs 1792 tests, 0 fail (macOS; was 1701), in 7 s (was 26 s). Wave 2 starts once these merge.
- [x] #406 apply `require_approval` gate fails open on quoted values → PR #431
- [x] #407 private-watch closes tracking issues for repos it could not read → PR #430
- [x] #408 onboard: declined PRs and unreadable CLAUDE.md → PR #432

- [x] #410 roadmap provenance accepts issue refs and ref-less entries → PR #436
- [x] #411 remove fabricated ROADMAP.md entries (merge while no roadmap PR is open) → PR #433
- [x] #412 config and schema truth → PR #434
- [x] #413 MCP tests deterministic → PR #437

### Wave 2 — structure (after wave 1 merges)
Status 2026-09-27: all seven MERGED after independent review. Reviews also found and fixed a pre-existing private-repo guard gap (#450) and a repo-cache that never hit (#449 → PR #451, merged 2026-09-27).

openIssues.title: decision: does the IDEATE → council → PROPOSE soak earn its keep?
openIssues.body:
Verdict needed; council/propose refactors are parked behind it.

- `snapshots/propose-soak.json`: 14 weekly entries since 2026-06-23, 32 ideas, 0 cross-repo routes (no-target 19, not-allowlisted 6, no-finding-anchor 6).
- The council approved 3/3 on 2026-09-21, including one that re-proposes shipped #400; the same idea recurred four weeks running in August.

openIssues.title: decision: keep, repair or remove the monitor phase
openIssues.body:
Verdict needed; the cursor fix is parked behind it.

- Monitor watches only repo-butler itself, 4x/day, and spends deep-provider tokens triaging; `context.triageResult` is read by nothing, the persisted cursor holds IDs only, and MCP `get_monitor_events` returns counts, never events.
- Its cursor also forgets known IDs (`monitor.js:300-335`): a 4-run harness showed every open alert and release re-sent to the council every 12 h.

Recommendation: remove (`monitor.js`, `monitor.yml`, the MCP tool, `triageEvents`, agent-card entry). If kept, it first needs a consumer, then the fix: store all currently open IDs, carry the previous set forward on a failed fetch, test 4 runs with a failure in run 3.

openIssues.title: decision: is repo-butler a reusable Action or an own-portfolio tool?
openIssues.body:
Verdict needed; blocks the README Usage section and any action.yml work.

- `action.yml`'s hyphenated inputs are never read (runner exports `INPUT_DRY-RUN`; `index.js` reads `INPUT_DRY_RUN`), so a `uses:` run has no token and exits. No workflow here uses `action.yml`, and code search finds no external consumer.
- `@v1` points at v1.0.0, whose code defaults to LIVE; fixing inputs without setting the action's `dry-run` default to `'true'` in the same commit would flip consumers live, and live consumer runs include auto-onboard PRs pointing at this owner's Pages site.

Recommendation: declare it an own-portfolio tool — trim action.yml inputs and README Usage to a "run it on your portfolio" section. If supported instead: read both input spellings failing closed, default dry-run true, gate onboard to the owner, then float `@v1` in `release.yml`.

openIssues.title: Agentic lockfile fix for the cases lockfile-update refuses: daily flow on docker agent (spike first)
openIssues.body:
## Summary
A daily agentic flow to clear the npm lockfile alerts that the deterministic `lockfile-update` tool (PR #400, ADR-015) refuses or fails on: npm `ERESOLVE`, split co-versioned pairs (vitest + `@vitest/coverage-v8`, `codeql-action` init + analyze), peer conflicts, and gate refusals such as `out-of-family` or `release-line-crossing`. It is not a replacement for PR #400, which handles the mechanical `reachable-by-update` case with no model at all; on 2026-09-16 that case covered five of five fixes done by hand. This flow is the judgment residue, and it should start only where the deterministic tool has reported a refusal or an npm error.

## Design principle
The agent proposes a diff; code decides whether it ships. The agent step holds no GitHub token and works on a checkout with `persist-credentials: false`, returning a structured verdict. A separate step runs the deterministic gate from PR #400 (`computeLockfileGate` in `src/lockfile-update.js`) over the working tree, and only if the gate passes does a further step holding the App token commit, push and open the PR. This maps onto ADR-005: the LLM never participates in the write decision. It needs an ADR in the ADR-013 mould because it is the first flow where a model chooses the operation on a file the butler did not author.

## Runtime: docker agent, verified facts (v1.140.0, 2026-09-15)
- `github.com/docker/docker-agent` (formerly cagent) publishes a standalone `docker-agent-linux-amd64` on GitHub releases; no Docker Desktop needed; no checksum files published; releases roughly daily.
- `provider: google` reads `GEMINI_API_KEY`, which this repo already has as a secret.
- `--exec` runs headless; `--json` emits one NDJSON event per line; `--safety restricted` is the fail-closed headless mode (safe calls run, everything else is denied, never prompts); `permissions` allow/deny rules with argument matching win over the mode.
- The `script` toolset exposes predefined commands as named tools with JSON-Schema typed args, so the agent cannot compose shell.
- `structured_output` with `mode: tool` lets the agent call tools and then deliver a schema-validated final answer (two reminders, then `structured_output_failed`).
- `TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false` disables telemetry.
- `docker agent eval` replays recorded sessions with deterministic assertions (`tool_called`, `contains`) and `--baseline` exits non-zero on regression, without its LLM judge.
- docker agent's own headless guide says permission pattern lists are defence in depth, not a boundary; `sbx` sandboxing is not on `ubuntu-latest`; a CI job's safety should rest on least-privilege secrets, `persist-credentials: false` and an ephemeral runner. The design below follows that.

## Agent definition (checked in, not pulled from a registry)
```yaml
# .github/agents/lockfile-fix.yaml
version: "15"
runtime:
  safety: restricted
models:
  gemini:
    provider: google
    model: gemini-3.5-flash
    thinking_budget: none
  claude:
    provider: anthropic
    model: claude-sonnet-4-6            # swap-in for the eval comparison; needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
agents:
  root:
    model: gemini
    description: Clears one transitive npm vulnerability alert with a lockfile-only change
    instruction_file: prompts/lockfile-fix.md   # the by-hand recipe, with refusal rules
    max_iterations: 15
    max_consecutive_tool_calls: 3
    add_environment_info: false
    toolsets:
      - type: script
        shell:
          inspect:
            cmd: node /butler/scripts/analyse.js ${pkg}
            description: Report direct, dev, override and locked versions of a package across manifests
            args: { pkg: { type: string, pattern: "^(@[a-z0-9._-]+/)?[a-z0-9._-]+$" } }
            required: [pkg]
          update_lockfile:
            cmd: npm update ${pkg} --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts
            description: Refresh the lockfile entry for one package within its existing range
            args: { pkg: { type: string, pattern: "^(@[a-z0-9._-]+/)?[a-z0-9._-]+$" } }
            required: [pkg]
          lockfile_diff:
            cmd: node /butler/scripts/vdiff.js
            description: Show every changed packages[].version between HEAD and the working tree
          dry_install:
            cmd: npm ci --dry-run --ignore-scripts
            description: Prove the lockfile resolves
    structured_output:
      mode: tool
      name: lockfile_fix_result
      schema:
        type: object
        additionalProperties: false
        properties:
          alert: { type: integer }
          package: { type: string }
          outcome: { type: string, enum: [updated, refused] }
          from: { type: string }
          to: { type: string }
          refusal_reason: { type: string, enum: [needs-override, needs-parent-major, eresolve, unknown, ""] }
          pr_summary: { type: string, maxLength: 600 }
        required: [alert, package, outcome, refusal_reason, pr_summary]
permissions:
  deny:
    - "shell"
    - "*:pkg=*&&*"
    - "*:pkg=*;*"
    - "*:pkg=*|*"
```

## Workflow skeleton
```yaml
# .github/workflows/agent-lockfile-fix.yml  (workflow_dispatch; inputs: repo, alert, dry-run=true)
- uses: actions/checkout@<sha>                      # repo-butler, for scripts/ and the agent YAML
  with: { path: butler, persist-credentials: false }
- uses: actions/checkout@<sha>                      # the target repo, read-only
  with: { repository: IsmaelMartinez/${{ inputs.repo }}, path: target, persist-credentials: false }
- name: Install docker-agent (pinned)
  run: |
    curl -sSL -o docker-agent https://github.com/docker/docker-agent/releases/download/v1.140.0/docker-agent-linux-amd64
    echo "<sha256 computed once and recorded here>  docker-agent" | sha256sum -c
    chmod +x docker-agent
- name: Run the agent                               # no GitHub token in this step's env
  working-directory: target
  env: { GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}, TELEMETRY_ENABLED: "false" }
  run: |
    printf '%s\n' "$FINDING_JSON" \
      | ../docker-agent run --exec --json --safety restricted ../butler/.github/agents/lockfile-fix.yaml - \
      > ../agent-events.ndjson
- name: Deterministic gate                          # the only thing that decides whether a PR exists
  run: node butler/scripts/lockfile-gate.js --alert "$ALERT" --result agent-events.ndjson --tree target
- name: Open PR                                     # App token minted here and only here; skipped on dry-run
  if: inputs.dry-run == 'false'
- uses: actions/upload-artifact@<sha>
  if: always()
  with: { name: agent-transcript, path: agent-events.ndjson }
```
`scripts/lockfile-gate.js` is a thin CLI over `computeLockfileGate` from PR #400: it reads `HEAD:package-lock.json` and the working tree's, checks that `git diff --name-only` is exactly `package-lock.json`, applies the same rules (manifest unchanged, every copy of the alert package at or above its patch, every change inside the alert packages' dependency closure and release line), and exits non-zero on refusal. The model's `pr_summary` is the only text that reaches GitHub, and it passes `validateIssueBody` first.

## Gates
The inherited ADR-005 gates are `workflow_dispatch` first, dry-run default (agent and gate run, the PR step does not), `require_approval`, one repo per run, and `REPO_NAME_PATTERN` on inputs. The three added gates are: no GitHub token in the agent step; the gate script is the sole write decision; and private repos are excluded by construction because the transcript artifact and the Actions log are world-readable on this public repo.

## Daily target and graduation
The flow starts as a manual dispatch and graduates to a daily cron only after the Track A stage-4 condition (several human-reviewed PRs merged over several weeks with no rollbacks) via a reviewed config change. Every session is recorded and `docker agent eval` is run against the recorded sessions as the soak evidence. The same YAML with `model: claude` on the same recorded findings answers whether Gemini Flash is good enough as the agent, which delegate-local's ADR 0031 identified as the only variable that moves quality.

## Risks
Binary supply chain: pin the version and a self-computed SHA-256, and disable auto-update in non-interactive sessions (the env var is in the install docs; verify its name before relying on it). Telemetry is on by default: set `TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false`. Whether `${pkg}` interpolation into a script `cmd` is shell-quoted is undocumented, so args are constrained with a pattern, compounds are denied, and `analyse.js` revalidates its argument. Prompt-injection exposure is low because the target repos are the owner's own, but the finding JSON on stdin must be built by the butler, never copied from advisory text. Gemini's free tier is 250 requests per day and a 15-iteration run is at most 15; count before any schedule.

## Alternatives to compare
Claude Code Action uses the same skeleton with one line swapped, and the recipe already exists as the `repo-butler-apply` skill, but it costs Claude API. Copilot coding agent has the butler file the finding as an issue and assign it, requiring zero infrastructure, but the gate then runs as a check after the PR exists rather than before. docker agent is the one that keeps the runs-for-free principle with Gemini and gives the recorded-session eval runner, so it is the first to try.

## Handover
This issue is for a fresh session. The case set starts from the 2026-09-16 refusals (yourear vitest 4 to 5 `ERESOLVE`, ismaelmartinez.me.uk `codeql-action` split pair, the TypeScript 7 holds) plus whatever PR #400's dry-run reports as gate refusals or npm errors once merged. Do it as a throwaway spike branch first, in the shape of delegate-local's `worktree-spike-agent-frameworks`, and let the eval table decide before any ADR is written.

Refs: ADR-005, ADR-013, ADR-015, PR #400, delegate-local ADR 0031

openIssues.title: CALCIO '90: 7.2's expert win-rate floor has less slack than its own sampling error
openIssues.body:
## The finding

7.2's `expert` win-rate floor at d = 0.25 is now the binding constraint on *any* improvement to the CPU's defence, and it has about five matches of slack in three hundred. It has already stopped two candidate fixes for #308, and it very nearly stopped the one that shipped.

Measured, `expert` win rate at d = 0.25 over 300 matches, against a floor of 0.800:

| build | win rate | matches |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (before #308's fix) | 0.8167 | 245 / 300 |
| `HEADER_SPREAD` 6 → 10 | 0.7833 | 235 |
| defensive header, any aerial ball in the box | 0.7867 | 236 |
| defensive header, opponent crosses only, p = 0.35 | 0.7967 | 239 |
| **shipped** (opponent crosses only, p = 0.28) | pass | — |

The shipped fix clears the floor only because the gate was narrowed *and* the probability lowered. Neither on its own was enough.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a note

There is a second problem underneath it. At 300 matches a win rate near 0.82 carries a standard error of about 0.022, which is **6.6 matches** — larger than the 5 matches of slack the floor is enforcing. So the floor is being asserted at a precision finer than the sample can resolve: a build can fail it, or pass it, for reasons that are inside the noise.

That showed up concretely while fixing #308. The first rolled version failed at 0.7967, six matches under the baseline — but adding an `m.rng()` draw also reshuffles the whole random stream, so part of that six was a reseeding rather than an effect, and there was no way to tell how much. The value had to be re-swept against the floor directly rather than reasoned about, which works but is expensive and does not generalise.

## What would close this

One of three, and the choice is a decision rather than a measurement:

1. **Give the floor headroom** — decide the easiest rung is allowed to get harder now that the CPU defends crosses, and restate the floor at a value the current build clears with more than its own sampling error.
2. **Deepen the sample** for this cell so the floor can resolve what it asserts, and record the CI cost against the #287 budget.
3. **Leave it as is**, explicitly, on the grounds that a tight floor at the easiest difficulty is the point — in which case the ticket closes as won't-do with the numbers above attached, so the next round starts after them.

The one thing that must not happen quietly is (1) as a side effect of some future PR that finds the floor inconvenient. That is the move the backlog plan's own rule forbids: nothing reaches green by relaxing a bound.

## Evidence

- `AIR_WIN_CHANCE` in `src/games/football/match.ts` carries the full sweep.
- `tests/games/football-balance.test.ts:150` is the assertion.
- PR #327 and issue #308 for the round this came out of.

openIssues.title: Line Hold: making a mid-campaign wave cost anything is a rebalance, not a constant
openIssues.body:
Split out of #263, whose readability half is fixed in PR #324. This is the stakes half, with the measurements that show why it is not a tuning pass.

## The fact, now pinned

`tests/games/towerdefense.test.ts` carries `only the finale costs the player anything, and only warlords do it (#263)`. A competent line holds 17 of 18 waves and leaks only warlords, only on wave 18. The test is mutation-checked (brute hp 110 to 400 turns it red), so a future balance change cannot move this silently.

## Why the obvious fixes do not work

**The margin is uniform, not slack.** Tracking the deepest marcher's progress along the route, on a line built as the run pays for it rather than handed over:

```
w 1 towers= 3 hp=x1.00 deepest=47%    w10 towers=10 hp=x2.31 deepest=21%
w 2 towers= 4 hp=x1.14 deepest=22%    w11 towers=11 hp=x2.60 deepest=24%
w 3 towers= 5 hp=x1.28 deepest=45%    w12 towers=11 hp=x2.99 deepest=44%
w 4 towers= 6 hp=x1.42 deepest=45%    w13 towers=12 hp=x3.48 deepest=45%
w 5 towers= 6 hp=x1.56 deepest=21%    w14 towers=13 hp=x4.07 deepest=25%
w 6 towers= 7 hp=x1.70 deepest=43%    w15 towers=13 hp=x4.76 deepest=51%
w 7 towers= 9 hp=x1.84 deepest=47%    w16 towers=13 hp=x5.55 deepest=42%
w 8 towers= 9 hp=x1.98 deepest=26%    w17 towers=15 hp=x6.44 deepest=52%
w 9 towers= 9 hp=x2.12 deepest=43%    w18 towers=15 hp=x7.43 deepest=100%
```

Nothing is drifting. The curve and the economy track each other for seventeen waves at a roughly 2x margin, and the finale is the one wave deliberately tuned to break through. The Round 6 contract in `waves.ts` says so outright: "even a maxed-out kill corridor cannot stop every crown".

**Difficulty is a step, not a slope**, because every marcher of a kind in a wave is identical and meets the same defence, so either all of them die in the corridor or all of them walk through. Sweeping a non-warlord toughness term (`hpScale` multiplied by `1 + late squared times k`, warlords exempt):

| k | brutes leaked | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | win, 15 lives |
| 0.005 to 0.016 | 0 | win, 5 lives (more *warlords* through, not brutes) |
| 0.02 | 4 to 7 | lost, or 1 life |
| 0.025 | 10 | lost |

There is no setting between "no consequence" and "overrun". This is also the mechanism behind the ticket's other observation, that tower count is non-monotonic past about twelve.

**Standard-bearers do not spread it.** One marcher in N spawning at a multiple of the hp was built and swept over share 3 to 8 and hp 2.2 to 6. Every cell changes how hard wave 18 hits (one warlord through becomes three or four) and none changes *which* waves hurt: all sixteen cells still held 17 of 18.

## What a real fix needs

Re-authoring the difficulty curve against the economy's growth curve so mid-campaign waves can bite, and re-deriving the no-perfect-runs contract that currently pins the finale as the only breach. Probably also giving a wave internal variance so a breach leaks a few marchers rather than the whole pack.

Worth weighing against the counter-argument first: a competent line holding everything until the finale is ordinary tower-defence design, and the 18 build policies the original audit measured were all decent ones. The ticket's premise is that this is a flaw; that premise is the thing to decide before spending a balance round on it.

Refs #263

openIssues.title: [parked] Pixel Park: rebuild the guest need selection and the score metric before reviving
openIssues.body:
Pixel Park is parked and fully unpublished (`src/pages/[lang]/fun/_park.astro`). The audit verdict is rebuild the simulation before reviving, on two structural findings. The ride graphics that were the stated reason for parking are a larger job than either.

1. An unserved need permanently masks every other need, so a park missing one building type earns nothing. `src/games/park/game.ts:649` takes `mostUrgentNeed(guest.needs)`, a single need (the lowest below 55, `guests.ts:52-60`), then scans only for buildings satisfying that one (`game.ts:653-657`). If none exists the guest wanders with a 30% chance of leaving (`game.ts:675`). It never tries the second-most-urgent need, and because the unserved need decays to 0 and stays lowest forever, the guest is locked out of spending on anything the park does offer.

Measured: a park with exactly one drink stall and a path network, run 20 in-game days, welcomed 121 guests and took 0 revenue. Not low, exactly zero. Per-need ablation, ten attractions, revenue per day over days 5-13, same seed: complete 739, no fun ride 0, no thrill ride 244, no food stall 80, no drink stall 57, no toilet 129. Severity tracks decay speed exactly, which is the signature of the masking.

Proposed fix, implemented and measured during the audit: in `chooseAction`, iterate the urgent needs in ascending order and take the first for which a reachable building exists. The lone drink stall goes from 0 to 15/day (upkeep 8, so viable as a first build should be); stalls-only goes 0 to 30/day (still loss-making against 52 upkeep, correct for a rideless park); and the complete park is unchanged at 823/day. Inert exactly where the park is well built.

2. In a well-run park guests never leave, so the score freezes and bigger parks score less. The score is `guestsWelcomed`, incremented only on spawn (`game.ts:579`), gated on `guests.length < maxGuests(day)` (`game.ts:887`, cap 120). A guest leaves only via happiness under 25 or the 30% roll after failing to find a building; in a park serving all five needs neither fires. Measured on a realistic staged build: welcomed sat at exactly 120 from day 25 to about day 70, eighteen real-time minutes in which the number being banked and submitted does not move. Same seeds, complete-need parks: 5 attractions scored 1,498; 8 scored 431; 10 scored 235; 15 and 20 scored 120. The best park scores twelve times less than the sloppiest. It also makes objective rung four ("welcome 400 guests", `objectives.ts:41`) unreachable for a strong park.

Not a one-liner: a 2-minute stay timer lifts admissions from 3.6/day to 11.0/day but drops the steady crowd from 120 to 51, which breaks the "draw a crowd of 90" prestige objective. Either a generous stay (4-5 min) with the crowd target lowered, or score something that grows monotonically with good play (lifetime revenue, guest-seconds).

3. Pacing is wrong for an arcade cabinet. Money bottoms at 15 on day 5 and never falls again until day 125, reaching 87k; bankruptcy arrives on day 237. That is about 3 minutes of tension, then 47 minutes at 1x where nothing can threaten you and nothing is left to buy, then a 45-minute slide into an unpreventable bankruptcy. Total run 94 minutes at 1x. The knob is `WAGE_RAMP = 1.4` at `economy.ts:50`.

Healthy and verified, for whoever picks this up: the 2x2 footprint machinery survived 27,503 successful mutations across 40 seeded maps with zero stranded annexes, zero overlaps and zero off-grid anchors; guest routing showed no leaks and no wedging; the scoring wiring itself is correctly gated. Also disproved: the coaster is NOT dominant - under paired seeds it beat the Pirate Ship by 1.6% with the sign flipping across seeds (noise) for 60% more cost, 31% more upkeep and four tiles instead of one. The instruction copy at `translations.ts:236` oversells it in all three locales.

Note the revival recipe in CLAUDE.md is stale: the floor now reads `UNLOCK_CHAIN` (`src/games/engine/progress.ts`) and `CABINETS` (`src/data/arcadeCabinets.ts`), so reviving is three edits, not two.

openIssues.title: [parked] Syndicate: the campaign arc inverts twice and progression rests on invisible weapon carryover
openIssues.body:
Measured with paired common random numbers, twelve seeds per cell, under a competent micro policy. Blocked behind the escort ticket, which must be fixed first.

1. The arc inverts twice. At pistol kit, mission 5 wins 4/12 while mission 6, billed as the decapitation finale, wins 9/12, because `assassinate` ends the moment the target dies whereas mission 5 requires walking the map recruiting ten civilians under minigun fire. At uzi kit the late run reads mission 7: 5/12, mission 8: 0/12, mission 9: 5/12; at minigun kit 12/12, 10/12, 12/12. Mission 8 (`src/games/syndicate/missions.ts:128-140`, seven uzi guards plus seven minigun enemies) is the hardest contract in the campaign on both kits, harder than the mission meant to escalate past it. Smallest fix: swap the specs for missions 8 and 9, or drop mission 8 enemies from 7 to 6.

2. Progression rests entirely on invisible weapon carryover. `rememberWeapons()` at `src/games/syndicate/game.ts:376-380` carries each surviving agent looted weapon into the next mission and silently resets dead agents to a pistol. Missions 8 and 9 win 0/12 on pistols and 10-12/12 on miniguns. A player who loses agents in mission 6 is quietly handed a mission 8 they cannot win, with nothing on screen explaining why. Smallest mitigation: show carried kit on the debrief screen, which already renders the next mission brief.

3. The civilian-casualty penalty is unreachable dead code. `game.ts:428-430` deducts 100 for a player-killed civilian, but player units only ever fire at victims drawn from the `hostiles` array (`sim.ts:252`), so a `kill` event with `kind: "civilian"` and `by: "player"` cannot be produced. Measured over 36 mission runs: 310 player kills (139 guards, 171 enemies), zero civilians. Forty-nine civilians died, all shot by hostiles, which carries no penalty. Collateral damage is the signature mechanic of the original and it is inert here.

Note the campaign is ten missions, not the nine CLAUDE.md claims.

Found by the August 2026 playability audit.

releases.name: v1.0.0
releases.body:
WiFi Sentinel v1.0.0 — multi-persona WiFi and network security analyser.

Features:
- CLI scanner with 10 scanner modules and three-tier tool fallback
- Five AI-style persona agents (red team, blue team, compliance, net engineer, privacy)
- Compliance scoring against CIS Wireless, NIST 800-153, IEEE 802.11, OWASP IoT
- WiFi RF intelligence: channel maps, saturation scoring, rogue AP detection
- External reconnaissance: DNS, TLS, headers, WHOIS, cert transparency
- Next.js dashboard with scan history, trends, persona perspectives
- HTML report export from CLI and dashboard
- Scan persistence with history, trend, and diff commands
- Scheduled scanning via launchd/cron
- Local OUI database (no external API calls)
- Linux support
- 44 unit tests, ESLint, GitHub Actions CI

openIssues.title: Tracking: simplification and reliability plan
openIssues.body:
## Summary
Plan from the 2026-09-27 review. Work top to bottom, one PR per issue; tick items here as they merge. `ROADMAP.md` mirrors this list.

## Plan
Phase 0 — fix what visitors see
- [ ] #218 CSP commented out in production (+ self-host ORT)
- [ ] #219 Model updater: wrong sizes, swallowed 429s, auto-merge
- [ ] #220 Clean up misleading models.json entries (after #219)
- [ ] #221 Deep links and small UI bugs

Phase 1 — data model
- [ ] #222 Flat, schema-validated models.json

Phase 2 — code
- [ ] #223 Remove dead code, lazy-load the classifier

Phase 3 — tests
- [ ] #224 Test the production classifier, decouple from live data

Phase 4 — docs and CI
- [ ] #225 Consolidate docs, make the project reusable
- [ ] #226 CI hardening

openIssues.title: CI hardening: npm ci, pinned actions, failing OSV scan

labels.name: github_actions
labels.description: Pull requests that update GitHub Actions code

openIssues.body:
## Problem
Workflows use npm install and floating action tags, the updater job holds write tokens while running install scripts, and the scheduled OSV scan keeps failing.

## Tasks
- [ ] `npm ci` in `deploy.yml` and `models-updater.yml` (`--ignore-scripts` in the updater, which holds write tokens)
- [ ] SHA-pin actions in deploy, models-updater, codeql and dependabot-auto-merge (release and osv-scanner already are)
- [ ] Concurrency groups on deploy and the updater
- [ ] Override `cookie` to ≥0.7.0; the scheduled OSV scan has failed five weeks running (GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x)
- [ ] `precompute-embeddings.js` should exit non-zero on failure
- [ ] Consider pinning `onnxruntime-web` to a stable release (currently 1.31.0-dev via transformers 4.3)

openIssues.title: Consolidate docs and make the project easier to reuse
openIssues.body:
## Problem
Documentation has grown to 37 files that repeat and contradict each other and the code, and an outsider has no quick way to understand, use or reuse the project.

## Tasks
- [ ] Cut 37 docs / 6,185 lines to README, ROADMAP, CONTRIBUTING, `docs/model-data.md`, `environmental-methodology.md` and ADRs
- [ ] Merge `project-status.md` and `project-vision.md` into `ROADMAP.md`
- [ ] Delete `docs/plans` (finished Phase 2), archive `docs/research`
- [ ] Fix false claims: "<50KB bundle", "98.3%", "LLM suite", `EnvironmentalImpactCalculator` as the implementation (CLAUDE.md); 2 AM vs 3 AM schedule; 7 vs 4 categories in `data-structure.md`
- [ ] Mark ADR-0002 superseded; add an ADR for the edge pivot
- [ ] README: example query, screenshot, shareable `?category=&task=` URLs, "add a model" steps
- [ ] GitHub description (mentions "benchmarks, cost") and topics
- [ ] `.nvmrc` + `engines`; `"test": "vitest run"`
- [ ] Delete flat `.claude/skills/*.md` (wrong layout, don't load) and duplicated `.claude/commands`

openIssues.title: Test the production classifier and decouple tests from live data
openIssues.body:
## Problem
The production classifier path is untested, the advertised 98.3% accuracy cannot be reproduced, and several tests depend on live models.json contents that the daily updater changes.

## Tasks
- [ ] Leave-one-out accuracy test over `reference-embeddings.json` with a floor. Measured 95.3% category / 75.0% subcategory; docs claim 98.3%, which is not reproducible (harness removed in 86a6a51)
- [ ] Stub-embedder unit tests for `EmbeddingTaskClassifier.classify` (the production path has 0% coverage; classification tests only hit the keyword fallback)
- [ ] Assert `reference-embeddings.json` texts match `tasks.json` examples; remove the silent skip in `precomputed-embeddings.test.js:8-11`
- [ ] Move ranking assertions tied to live data (`code-assistant.test.js:137,167,222`) to fixtures so data updates can't break the gate
- [ ] Remove vacuous assertions (e.g. `integration.test.js:222` `>= 0`)
- [ ] Consolidate the 10 test files into 4
- [ ] Later: one Playwright smoke test

openIssues.title: Remove dead code and lazy-load the embedding classifier
openIssues.body:
## Problem
The application contains approximately 500–700 lines of unused code and eagerly loads the entire machine learning stack on every visit, despite the fact that most visitors never utilise the free-text classifier.

## Tasks
- [ ] Delete unused code (~500–700 lines): `EnvironmentalImpactCalculator.js`, `classifierConfig.js`, `src/index.js`, `src/hooks.server.js`, `public/`, `scripts/generate-icons.js` + `@resvg/resvg-js`, the never-populated ensemble UI, unused classifier methods
- [ ] Shrink `EmbeddingTaskClassifier` (static JSON import, top-k vote) and cut `BrowserTaskClassifier` to a small keyword fallback
- [ ] Dynamic `import()` of the classifier / transformers.js only when "Describe your task" opens (today ~216 KB gzip initial JS, ~52 MB on first visit)
- [ ] Round embeddings to 4 decimals and ship as static JSON (2.6 MB → ~260 KB gzip); re-check accuracy
- [ ] Svelte 5 syntax (`npx sv migrate svelte-5`)
- [ ] Move the aggregator from `src/lib/aggregation` to `scripts/update-models/` and drop dead options
- [ ] Service worker: versioned cache name and eviction (cache grows without limit today)
- [ ] Self-host the font (Google Fonts leaks visitor IPs on a privacy-branded site)

Decision: keep MiniLM but lazy-load it (recommended), or go keyword-only.

openIssues.title: Simplify models.json to a flat, schema-validated list
openIssues.body:
## Problem
The category → subcategory → tier nesting stores derived facts (tier, environmental score) as structure. That forces duplicates when a model serves several tasks and lets tier contradict size (54 entries today).

## Tasks
- [ ] Flat `models` array; each model lists its `tasks`
- [ ] Derive tier and environmental score from `sizeMB` at load time
- [ ] Add `browserModelId` (ONNX mirror) and a CI check that it has `.onnx` files
- [ ] `accuracy` → null or `{metric, value, source}`; hide the accuracy filter until real data exists
- [ ] `models.schema.json` enforced in `npm test` (enums, ISO dates, unique ids, no placeholder ids)
- [ ] Decide on the xlarge tier (drop, or hide by default as out of scope for "no server")
- [ ] Publish `models.json` as a static asset with a documented schema so others can reuse it

openIssues.title: Deep links wait for the classifier download, plus small UI bugs
openIssues.body:
## Problem
Small user-facing bugs found while reviewing the live site and the page code.

## Tasks
- [ ] `+page.svelte:83` awaits `taskClassifier.initialize()` before handling `?category=&task=`, so shared links wait for the ~23 MB model. Handle params first; don't await init
- [ ] Deep links show results but the dropdowns stay on "Select a category…"

openIssues.title: Model updater writes wrong sizes, swallows HF 429s and auto-merges before CI
openIssues.body:
## Problem
The daily updater is the source of most bad data on the live site.

- `ModelAggregator.js:517` reads `safetensors.total` as a parameter count. For Ornith-1.0-35B that is 664944 while `parameters.BF16` is 35107181936, so it is listed as a 1 MB lightweight model. The detail fetch lacks `?blobs=true`, so the sibling-size path never runs.
- No `HF_TOKEN` in CI; a run makes ~700 calls against a 500 req / 5 min limit. 429s return null silently and the run still reports success.
- `extractAccuracy` invents accuracy from the model name (0.85 for "large", 0.75 default); 118/158 entries carry these values.
- `models-updater.yml` auto-merges ~4 s after opening the PR, before checks finish (e.g. #215).

## Tasks
- [ ] Size from `safetensors.parameters` × dtype or the weight file size via `?blobs=true`
- [ ] Retry 429 with backoff, fail the run when more than N% of detail calls fail, add the `HF_TOKEN` secret
- [ ] Stop inventing accuracy (write null)
- [ ] Remove auto-merge, run weekly, PR body summarises adds / removes / size changes
- [ ] Refresh existing entries instead of always keeping the stale copy (dedup around :777)

openIssues.title: CSP is commented out in production; enforcing it will break the classifier
openIssues.body:
## Problem
Since #180 the comment in `src/app.html` contains the literal `%sveltekit.head%`. SvelteKit injects the head (including the CSP `<meta>`) inside that comment, a hydration marker closes it early, and the comment tail plus a raw `%sveltekit.head%` render as page text. The live site currently has no CSP. Fixing only the comment would silently break the embedding classifier: the ORT wasm/mjs load from `cdn.jsdelivr.net` and the model weights redirect to `us.aws.cdn.hf.co`, neither of which the policy allows.

## Tasks
- [ ] Remove `%sveltekit.head%` from the comment in `src/app.html` (also drop the no-op `X-Content-Type-Options` meta and the duplicate old description meta)
- [ ] Self-host ORT by setting `env.backends.onnx.wasm.wasmPaths` to the bundled asset (the 26.8 MB wasm is already deployed but unused)
- [ ] Add `https://*.hf.co` to `connect-src` in `svelte.config.js`
- [ ] Verify on a preview build with the CSP enforced: classifier loads, no console violations

openIssues.title: git resolver clones a repository once per ref instead of once
openIssues.body:
## Current behaviour
The `cloneOnce()` function in `src/resolvers/git.js` memoises clones keyed on the combination of repository and reference. Consequently, a manifest that names the same repository under several references (such as `main`, a release tag, or a pinned SHA) performs one full blobless network clone for each distinct reference. Although SHA-pinned references already produce a wide clone containing every branch and tag, a sibling entry at `main` still triggers its own separate clone.

## Cost
This behaviour results in unnecessary network traffic and redundant cloning operations. It specifically affects manifests that reference multiple refs of a single repository, as each distinct ref incurs a full clone cost rather than reusing the existing wide clone.

## Possible directions
Two potential fixes are identified. The first is to key the cache on the repository alone and use `git fetch origin <ref>` into the existing clone on a cache miss. The second is to take the wide clone once and let the existing `git log <ref> -- path` and `ls-tree <ref>` calls select the ref, as these commands already name the ref explicitly.

## Priority
This issue is not urgent. It was found during a quality review pass rather than being identified as a behaviour bug, and it only affects manifests with multiple refs of one repository.

releases.name: v0.1.0 — Repository Strategist
releases.body:
First release of the Repository Strategist — a GitHub App that maintains institutional memory for software projects and uses it to provide doc-grounded triage and strategic intelligence.

## Features

- Multi-phase triage pipeline: deterministic template parsing (Phase 1), vector search + Gemini suggestions (Phase 2), enhancement context briefs (Phase 4a)
- Synthesis engine: weekly cluster detection, ADR drift detection, upstream impact analysis, posted as shadow repo briefings
- Enhancement research agent: mirror issues in shadow repos, context briefs, full research synthesis with safety gates
- MCP server: four tools exposing triage, synthesis, health, and trend data to Claude Code agents
- Event journal: records all repo activity for temporal analysis
- Auto-ingest: re-embeds changed documentation on push
- Per-repo config via `.github/butler.json`
- Live dashboard at `/dashboard`
- Two-layer safety: structural validator + LLM reviewer on all outputs
- Shadow repo approval gates: `lgtm`/`reject` for triage, `research`/`use as context`/`reject` for enhancements

## Infrastructure

Go 1.26.1 on Google Cloud Run, Neon PostgreSQL with pgvector, Gemini 2.5 Flash, GitHub Actions CI/CD with Workload Identity Federation.

## Documentation

- 13 Architecture Decision Records in `docs/adr/`
- Roadmap with six streams in `docs/plans/2026-03-04-roadmap.md`
- Security policy in `SECURITY.md`

releases.body:
# @ismaelmartinez/generator-atlassian-compass-event-catalog

## 0.3.0

### Minor Changes

-   feat: presentation layer improvements
    -   Populate `service.attachments` from Compass links via structured links (url, title, type, icon)
    -   Categorise links into subsections: Compass, Development, Operations, Documentation, Other
    -   Expose `StructuredLink` type and pass it as optional third parameter to custom markdown templates
    -   Surface `customFields` as a markdown table between Links and Dependencies sections
    -   Map Compass `typeId` to `service.styles.icon` using Lucide icon names

## 0.2.1

### Patch Changes

-   53a5fd2: fix: address security vulnerabilities in token logging, path traversal, and XSS
    -   Prevent potential API token leakage via error logs in team fetch failure handling
    -   Sanitize local spec file paths to reject path traversal sequences (`../`) and absolute paths
    -   Sanitize custom field text values from Compass API to prevent XSS in rendered markdown

## 0.2.0

### Minor Changes

-   a547fd4: feat: map Compass DEPENDS_ON relationships to service markdown
    -   Parse `relationships.DEPENDS_ON` from Compass YAML and resolve referenced services
    -   Add a "Dependencies" section to generated service markdown with links to dependent services
    -   Use a two-pass approach: first collect all services, then resolve dependencies between them
    -   Handle missing dependency targets gracefully (log warning, don't crash)
    -   Services without dependencies show "No known dependencies."

## 0.1.0

### Minor Changes

-   d3f5ee0: Modernize and fix core gaps (Phase 1)
    -   Replace local Service type with SDK's Service type for richer metadata support
    -   Map Compass lifecycle, tier, and labels to EventCatalog badges
    -   Map Compass repository links to service repository URL
    -   Map Compass ownerId to service owners
    -   Support updating existing services with overrideExisting option (defaults to true)
    -   Add Zod validation for generator configuration with clear error messages

-   26590b0: Support all Compass component types (Phase 2)
    -   Remove SERVICE-only restriction — all Compass types (APPLICATION, LIBRARY, CAPABILITY, CLOUD_RESOURCE, DATA_PIPELINE, MACHINE_LEARNING_MODEL, OTHER, UI_ELEMENT, WEBSITE) are now processed as EventCatalog services
    -   Add `typeFilter` option to selectively process only specified component types
    -   Add component type badge showing the Compass type (e.g. APPLICATION, LIBRARY) on each service

### Patch Changes

-   e6e0f5c: Phase 1: Update dependencies to latest versions

    -   @changesets/cli: ^2.28.1 → ^2.29.7
    -   chalk: ^5.4.1 → ^5.6.2

    All tests pass with updated dependencies. See UPDATE_PLAN.md for full modernization roadmap.

## 0.0.8

### Patch Changes

-   3c0a302: Updating depencencies and moving to eventcatalog/sdk 2.0.0

## 0.0.7

### Patch Changes

-   06e4c92: Fix docs and update the dependencies

## 0.0.6

### Patch Changes

-   5600c7a: fix chalk version to 4 to avoid ESM breaking changes

## 0.0.5

### Patch Changes

-   7bfa0ac: update dependencies and adding default PROJECT_DIR when not present

## 0.0.4

### Patch Changes

-   85cf3f5: update dependencies and improve documentation

### Patch Changes

releases.name: v1.1.0 — Curated Channels
releases.body:
## What's new

- 44 hand-picked channels (UK news, entertainment, movies, music, sports, kids, docs) as the default experience
- Automated channel validation script testing streams from iptv-org playlists
- Weekly GitHub Action keeps validation data fresh
- 1,800+ validated channels available via Find > Validated for discovery
- Split export buttons (All / Favs) to prevent accidental favourites-only export
- Wrapping category filter pills instead of horizontal scroll
- New channels highlight in sidebar when added from Find panel
- Community health files (code of conduct, issue/PR templates)

## Breaking changes

None — the app loads picks.json as the default channel list, falling back to the built-in list if offline.
